projects.title: mathlib4
projects.summary: A community-built library of mathematics for the Lean 4 proof assistant.
projects.description: Mathlib brings mathematical definitions, theorems, and proof tools together in a shared Lean library. Its source and generated documentation show how a large mathematical reference can develop through many individual contributions.
highlights: Mathematical definitions and theorem proofs in Lean 4
An example of a shared mathematical library

projects.title: The Stacks Project
projects.summary: An openly developed textbook and reference on algebraic geometry, with its mathematical source kept in Git.
projects.description: The Stacks Project connects a readable mathematical reference with a public source repository. Chapters, proofs, and stable tags make a growing body of exposition navigable. It illustrates how a living text can serve researchers without being organized around a single article.
highlights: A connected reference in algebraic geometry
Readable chapters backed by TeX source
projects.contributionNote: Consult the project's current website and contribution policies before suggesting a change. The repository is the source for current participation rules.
projects.licenseNote: The project's reuse terms are provided in the upstream COPYING file. MathStoa's license does not replace those terms.

projects.title: Liquid Tensor Experiment
projects.summary: A Lean project on results in the theory of liquid vector spaces.
projects.description: This repository records a Lean 3 formalization effort inspired by Peter Scholze's Liquid Tensor Experiment. It connects mathematical source material, intermediate results, and formal proofs in a shared project. It is included as a reference example of collaborative mathematical work.
highlights: Links between source mathematics and formal proofs
projects.contributionNote: Consult the repository for its current status and any successor work.
projects.licenseNote: Consult the upstream repository and referenced mathematical sources for reuse terms. MathStoa asserts no license over the linked work.
